key_insight: A vortex-beam transient absorption microspectroscopy (VTAM) method can resolve ultrafast free-exciton and polaron diffusion in 2D perovskites without spatial scanning or image reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: This gives a faster, simpler way to measure carrier transport parameters in perovskite optoelectronics, supporting better materials screening and device design.
method: Uses vortex pump-probe beams with different topological charges to encode spatial diffusion into the signal.
Extracts mode-dependent transient absorption dynamics with subpicosecond temporal resolution.
Fits the data with a time-dependent diffusion model to separate transient and steady-state transport.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a transient diffusion enhancement of 68.84 cm2/s, a steady-state diffusion coefficient of 1.85 cm2/s, an initial diffusion coefficient of 70.69 cm2/s, and a cooling time of 0.35 ps, while EP resonance showed strongly suppressed diffusion.
watch_item: The method relies on accurate vortex-beam alignment, resonance selection, and model fitting, so robustness across different perovskite compositions and experimental setups still needs validation.
paper_title: Vortex-Beam Transient Absorption Microspectroscopy Resolves Ultrafast Free-Exciton and Polaron Diffusion in 2D Perovskites
